Subject: MAP kickoff + deployment/region ask

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loved the latency numbers. We need to get a Mutual Action Plan in place so we can land an exec sign-off and procurement letter by the end of April. Two asks to start the MAP: 1) we'd like a recommendation for deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for a PHI-containing assistant; 2) we need a proposed evaluation plan and timeline tied to those deployment options so our security and procurement teams can budget appropriately.

High-level constraints:
- Processing includes PHI (patient notes) => HIPAA scope
- Target peak QPS: ~20 requests/sec; expected avg tokens per call ~600
- Preferred region: us-east for latency, but we may need multi-region later
- Required SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime and <300ms latency P95 for short prompts

Please attach a MAP PDF and a short checklist we can share with security & procurement.

Also cc'ing Sam (engineering lead) who will own the evaluation. Sam — feel free to drop any immediate technical must-haves.

Best,
Priya
Dr. Priya Singh
Head of Clinical AI, MedVana Health

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + deployment/region ask

Hi Priya — thanks for laying this out. I attached a draft MAP and a separate evaluation checklist that maps tests to deployment modes. High-level guidance up-front:

- Recommendation: Dedicated for initial production (HIPAA + predictable throughput). Hosted can be used for early-stage evals but requires a BAA and region constraints; Private would be recommended if you need on-prem or full air-gap (typically later-stage or regulated partners).
- Region: start us-east (we can pin nodes there), with a multi-AZ plan and optional secondary region (us-west) for DR.
- Evaluation plan (summary): 2-week PoC (staging traffic + synthetic PHI workload) -> 1-week canary at 10% -> full cutover. We included acceptance criteria tied to latency, error rate, and cost/unit.

I've looped in Karthik for the technical acceptance criteria and Laura for the customer success checkpoints and go/no-go cadence. Next steps:
1) Sam: confirm RPS patterns (burst vs steady) and any egress constraints for the PII pipeline.
2) Priya: if procurement can share payment terms cadence we can map milestones in the MAP (we typically align invoicing to canary + full roll).
3) Karthik: can you add the SLO numbers and the test endpoints in the MAP?

Attachments: MedVana_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP), evaluation_checklist.csv

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min call today if that helps.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MedVana_MAP_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

On Tue, Mar 2, 2027 at 11:03 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I've looped in Karthik for the technical acceptance criteria and Laura for the customer success checkpoints and go/no-go cadence.

Thanks — quick technical notes and a suggested evaluation plan from the SE side:

- Deployment guidance: Dedicated (GPU-backed reservations) with customer VPC peering and pinned model version; this gives predictable P95 and isolates PHI. Hosted with a BAA is possible for evals but may introduce cold-start variability. Private (on-prem) only if MedVana requires full control of keys and air-gapped network; that adds ~6–8 weeks for on-prem packaging.
- Instance sizing: for 20 QPS and ~600 tokens per call we recommend 4x A100-equivalent GPUs with the following batching profile and KV cache sizing (details in the MAP attachment).
- Test harness / acceptance criteria (included in eval checklist):
  * Latency: P95 < 300ms on 95% of runs with production data mix
  * Throughput: sustain 20 QPS for 30 minutes with <5% tail amplification
  * Quality: ROUGE/F1 on synthetic clinical prompts within 2% of baseline
  * Security: SOC2 artifacts uploaded (we provided a redacted copy) + egress test (no external exfiltration)
- Region specifics: we can provision pinned capacity in us-east-1 (primary) and warm capacity in us-west-2 for DR; cross-region replication of KV cache is not automatic — we recommend a short failover window for DR.

I attached a redacted SOC2 for security to help procurement. I'll also drop a short-runbook and the SE-run test endpoints into the shared Drive.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2_redacted_2026.pdf (application/pdf)]
